summary: A Google Doc, Sheet, Slides or Drive link posted in a room is now recorded as a link handle, and in the conversation she reads Nora sees a handle such as [Google Doc link c41d09] in the link's place, not the raw URL.
details: Works on every platform. Recording a link makes no network call and needs no Google account; the message is stored exactly as it was sent.
The handle replaces the link in the conversation Nora answers, in her transcript and memory-search tool results, in what is newly fed to memory, and in what memory hands back to her.
Links already in the message record were recorded the same way when this was installed, so their handles resolve.
The operator's review channel still shows the link as posted, so it stays clickable.
The same file posted twice gets the same handle. Folder links, Google Forms and published-to-web links stay ordinary links.
limitations: Nora cannot open a linked file yet; opening one comes in a later step and will need her own Google account.
Memory already holds links fed before this change as raw URLs. They are shown to Nora as handles when read back, but memory's own summaries may still have absorbed details from them.
A link added to a message by editing it shows as a handle but is not recorded with the message.
A handle resolves only among the messages of the room it was posted in.
